en: A Venus flytrap can count up to five touches on its sensory hairs before it finally snaps its trap shut.
Wombats produce cube-shaped feces to prevent them from rolling away when they mark their territory on rocks.
The human nose can distinguish and remember over one trillion different scents.
Adult mayflies typically live for only twenty-four hours because they lack functional mouthparts and cannot eat.
Trees share nutrients and warn each other of danger through an underground fungal network called mycorrhizae.
The axolotl can completely regenerate lost body parts, including its brain, heart, and limbs, without scarring.
A fever helps your body fight infections by creating a hot environment where harmful germs struggle to survive.
The mimic octopus can change its shape and behavior to impersonate over fifteen different toxic marine animals.
Just like fingerprints, every human has a completely unique tongue print that no one else shares.
A sloth can take up to a month to digest a single meal due to its extremely slow metabolism.
The Welwitschia plant can survive in the desert for over a thousand years using only two continuously growing leaves.
Your body produces roughly two million new red blood cells every single second to replace aging ones.
